newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat pleads with Israel to make peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat pleads with Israel to make peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat appealed to Israel to resume peace moves on Friday, saying it was the only way to put an end to three days of bloodshed.
"The peace process is the only way to work a way out of violence and killing and the attacks that are taking place," he told reporters in the self-ruled Gaza Strip.

Speaking after he met Yossi Sarid, head of an Israeli leftist opposition party, the Palestinian leader assailed the storming of Jerusalem's Temple Mount, site of al-Aqsa mosque, by Israeli police who killed three Palestinians.
"This is a violation of what we had agreed last night -- that we must calm the situation in Jerusalem," Arafat said.

Palestinian officials said that in a phone conversation early on Friday, Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu agreed to calm the atmosphere. Arafat said he also spoke by telephone with Israeli President Ezer Weizman.

"The attempt to attack worshippers in al-Aqsa mosque is something that we can never accept. I have just spoken with the president, Mr Weizman, and Mr Sarid, and explained to them the situation which we are suffering from," Arafat said.
